subject: Renewal: step-up proposal and throughput lane for Olive Retail
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@olive-retail.com>
Cc: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: step-up proposal and throughput lane for Olive Retail

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the thoughtful product session last week. Based on Olive's growth patterns and the spike in checkout routing at peak hours, we've put together a renewal proposal that increases your hosted monthly commit and adds a soft throughput lane to reduce soft-failure throttling during seasonal peaks. Attached is a short proposal PDF and a CSV of recent usage months.

High level:
- Current commit: 6M tokens/month
- Proposed step-up: 10M tokens/month (effective on renewal date)
- Burst/buffer: additional 2M tokens buffer (monthly, non-rolling) that can be applied during 3 peak days per month
- Soft throttle adjustments: increase per-route rate from 350 rps to 470 rps for the checkout route (same price tier)
- Pricing: blended rate for the first 12 months at $0.0018/token for committed usage, bursts billed at $0.0035/token

Operational notes:
- We will provision a dedicated pool for Olive's checkout route with traffic shaping rules to respect your latency SLOs.
- Auto-fallback to a smaller quantized model is available if sustained load breaches the buffer; we'll only activate after mutual notification.

Next steps:
1) Quick internal check so we can finalize the DocuSign link (I can send a version with or without the buffer language).
2) If you agree, sign and we target 2026-09-01 effective renewal.

Attaching: 2026-08-19_Olive_Retail_Renewal_Proposal.pdf, usage_history_q2-q3.csv

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20m call if useful.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Park <olivia@olive-retail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@olive-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: step-up proposal and throughput lane for Olive Retail

Hi Logan —

Appreciate the fast follow-up and the clear proposal. A couple quick clarifying questions before we loop in procurement: 

1) For the 2M buffer: is that a true monthly allowance (resets every month) or a one-time buffer for the first 3 months?
2) Can you confirm whether the soft throttle increase to 470 rps is per-route or global for our account? Our checkout route is the one that matters, but we run background enrichment that we don't want to inadvertently raise.
3) Do you have an estimated monthly cost delta using our past three months as a baseline? Happy to accept a range.

If everything looks reasonable we'll route to contracts — we typically need 7 business days for final signatures.

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Product, Olive Retail

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: step-up proposal and throughput lane for Olive Retail

Logan — quick internal note before I reply to Olivia:

Answers for the questions: 
- Buffer: the 2M is a recurring monthly buffer that resets at the start of each billing month. It is designed to cover predictable peaks and won't carry over. We can offer an alternative: one-time 6M buffer over the first 3 months if they prefer a ramped approach.
- Rate scope: we intended the 470 rps increase to apply only to the named checkout route (route-level QoS). We should call that out explicitly in the contract.
- Cost delta: based on their last 3 months, estimate ~+$7,200/month on committed usage (blended rate) plus potential burst spend depending on utilization; I pushed a short calc in the attached usage CSV.

Opportunities/asks: 
1) Marissa — can you prepare a short appendix (1 paragraph) about the dedicated pool ops SLA and how fallbacks will be triggered and communicated?
2) Logan — include explicit route names in the SOW; Contracts likes precise identifiers.

I'll draft a concise reply to Olivia and include the one-page appendix.

— Aisha
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@olive-retail.com>
Cc: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ethan_park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: step-up proposal and throughput lane for Olive Retail

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the questions. Short answers inline below, and I've attached an updated one-pager and an appendix from our operations lead.

1) Buffer: recurring monthly allowance that resets at calendar month boundary. If you prefer a front-loaded buffer (6M over first 3 months) we can offer that as an alternative; note pricing and burst rules stay the same.

2) Rate scope: route-level only. We'll include explicit route identifiers ("checkout/charge" and "checkout/confirm") in the SOW so background enrichment routes are unaffected.

3) Cost delta: estimating committed + buffer = ~$7,200/mo increase. If they hit the full 2M buffer each month and also use 10% bursts beyond that, total additional spend could range up to ~$13k/month — this is a conservative upper bound. See attached quick calc.

Operational appendix highlights (from Marissa):
- Dedicated pool will be provisioned 7 days prior to effective date.
- Automatic fallback to quantized model triggers only after buffer is exhausted and a sustained 5-minute queue depth threshold is reached; notification to Olive via PagerDuty + email precedes fallback by 60s when possible.
- All throttling/fallback events will be logged in Console with token-level traces and a post-incident summary within 48 hours.

I've produced two contract options in DocuSign: (A) recurring 2M monthly buffer; (B) front-loaded 6M buffer for first 3 months. Link: https://www.docusign.com/en/oliveretail/renewal-2026

If you give me a thumbs-up on option A or B I'll have Contracts prepare the final redline. Target effective date 2026-09-01 if signed by 2026-08-31.

Cheers,
Logan

From: Contracts Team <contracts@olive-retail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Olivia Park <olivia@olive-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: step-up proposal and throughput lane for Olive Retail

Logan / Aisha / Marissa —

Thanks — Contracts reviewed option A and we're comfortable with the recurring monthly buffer and the route-level scope. We have one small ask: can you add a 90-day SLA clause for post-activation capacity tuning (i.e., Redwood will provide a free tuning pass within the first 90 days to adjust QoS settings if real traffic differs materially from forecasts)? If yes we'll countersign and route to procurement today.

Olivia (for signature)

Regards,
Contracts Team
Olive Retail
